text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - Bund futures ended solidly higher as reports of slow, non-inflationary economic growth continued to support hopes for a cut in the repo rate. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.55, up 0.10 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilt futures ended firmer after an active session in which the March contract surged to a contract high of 111-28/32 after an unexpected drop in December retail sales. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 111-18/32, up 22/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures slipped back from a new contract high as Bunds and U.S. bonds failed to hold their gains. A growing feeling that the strong dollar could delay rate cuts led to a flattening of the curve. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 130.80 up 0.26 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures held to firmer levels in late afternoon but were off their record highs as profit taking tempered the market's opening enthusiasm following a Bank of Italy interest rate cut late Tuesday. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 131.90, up 0.17 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - The prices of U.S. Treasury securities opened in choppy trading following a weak housing starts report. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 111-09/32, down 07/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.79 percent.

JAPAN - Key March 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures closed firmer as the JGB market ignored a rebound in Tokyo stocks. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.16, up 0.16 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market saw a broad spectrum of currencies tapped amid active issuance. The Province of Quebec launched a $750 million 10-year global bond which will be priced to yield between 58 and 60 basis points over the 6.5 percent October 2006 U.S. Treasury on Thursday. The bond -- joint lead-managed by CSFB, Goldman Sachs, Merrill Lynch, Nomura and SBC Warburg -- was smaller than the anticipated $1.0 billion. Quebec is rated A2 by Moody's Investors Service and A+ by Standard & Poor's Corp.
